clue.text: Perks up on the brow?

parts.note: read whimsically as advantages sitting on the forehead, where a line of cut hair hangs; in fact perks are extras an employer gives on top of salary

explanation.surface: A question about what perks someone up when worn across the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Perks are the extras of a job beyond pay, which is the everyday sense of this phrase; the cryptic sense pictures hair hanging over the brow.

clue.text: Back to basics for good-time girl without an end to northern charm

parts.note: a good time is fun
dame is an old slang word for a woman or girl

indicators.note: the end of the word northern supplies its final letter
the charm is used without the two letters spelling an

parts.note: a talisman is a lucky charm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good-time girl lacks the northern charm to get back to basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good-time girl' looks like one phrase but gives two pieces; 'without an' works on the charm, not on the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentalism is a strict return to the founding principles of a creed, a going back to basics.

clue.text: Poetry is so reciprocal

definitions.meaning: poetry is written in lines of verse, so it is set down that way
in mathematics an ... quantity is the reciprocal, one over the number

explanation.surface: A remark that poetry is so mutual.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse and reciprocal are mathematical synonyms; poetry, by contrast, is composed in verse.

clue.text: Flower containing male element

indicators.note: the flower holds the male letter inside it

parts.note: the geranium is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A blossom with a male part to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a chemical element, a grey metalloid used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Abate when energy's sapped from under and above

indicators.note: energy is drained out of the word for under, so its letter is removed

parts.note: below means under
E is the physics symbol for energy
over means above

explanation.surface: Something calms down once energy is drained from underneath and on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm or quarrel that blows over dies down, the same as abating.

clue.text: Indicator of some aggravation

definitions.meaning: the pointer on a dial or compass
... is also bad feeling or provocation, as in a ... match

explanation.surface: Something that shows a bit of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge's pointer is a needle, and needle is British slang for antagonism or irritation.

clue.text: Harris put up a list of local plant life

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Rolf Harris was an Australian-born entertainer on British television

explanation.surface: Someone named Harris compiles a catalogue of the area's plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ROLF into FLOR in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A flora is the plant life of a region, and also a book or catalogue listing it.

clue.text: Cadet drops in aid for driver

indicators.note: the drops are placed inside the golfer's peg

parts.note: a golf tee holds up the ball for a shot with the club called a driver
rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A cadet abandons a teaching aid meant for motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist and learner driving, but here it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person in training, a learner or trainee.

clue.text: Making light of swimming centre with two shops

indicators.note: letters in the water move about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: two shops means the word for one shop taken twice

parts.note: a single shop counted twice gives the plural

explanation.surface: Making light of a swimming centre that has two shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorescent things glow, giving off light without heat.

clue.text: At no time to be always equal or less

definitions.meaning: never again, at no future time
something always equal or less is cryptically ... than

explanation.surface: A reflection on never being more than equal, or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raven's refrain means never again, at no time hereafter, while the cryptic reading is never more.

clue.text: Starters switched from fish to vegetable

indicators.note: the first two letters of the fish change places

parts.note: the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A diner swaps a fish starter for a vegetable one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters switched' swaps the opening R and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orach is a leafy plant eaten like spinach, a vegetable.

clue.text: Lobbies' atmosphere circulating after a time

indicators.note: the stirred-up atmosphere is placed after the a and time pieces
air moving round is rearranged

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: Hotel lobbies get fresh air circulating after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobbies'' with its apostrophe looks possessive, but it is the plural definition; the apostrophe just links to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are entrance halls or courts in buildings, the same thing as lobbies.

clue.text: Medium is plain to fancy

indicators.note: to fancy here is to dress up the letters in a new pattern

explanation.surface: An artist's chosen medium is made plain to anyone who likes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paints are an artist's medium, the material a picture is made in.

clue.text: Almost bawl to have a German queen going around in make-up

indicators.note: the German pieces surround the shortened shout

parts.note: ein is German for a

indicators.note: the last letter of the shout is lost

parts.note: to bawl is to yell
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Someone nearly cries when a German queen goes round wearing make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a German' is the German word for a; 'Almost' trims the shout's last letter and 'going around' wraps the German pieces about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is a cosmetic drawn along the eyelids, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Cutting-edge equipment's first used to crack problem

indicators.note: the opening letter breaks into the word for problem

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

indicators.note: the opening letter of equipment is taken

explanation.surface: The first piece of equipment is used to solve a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech means using advanced technology, which is what cutting-edge describes.

clue.text: Economic problem in what was used to decrease right away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken away from the old pressing tool

parts.note: a flatiron was used to remove creases, read as de-crease

explanation.surface: An economic problem involving what used to be used to cut things down quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decrease' is read as de-crease: take creases out, the job of an old flatiron. 'away' removes its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation, a general rise in prices, is a classic problem in economics.

clue.text: Sporting barrier that generates pots?

parts.note: the word stop written backwards gives the word pots

explanation.surface: A fence in sport that somehow produces pots.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstop is a fence or screen behind the playing area, or the fielder behind the batter, in baseball or rounders.

clue.text: Turn in a trading place brought back bad experience

indicators.note: the whole piece is read backwards
the turn goes inside the market piece

parts.note: a mart is a market
a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: A turn in a market brought back a bad memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside A MART to make AMUART, and 'brought back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a deeply distressing experience or the shock from it.

clue.text: Don't pick a second-grade mark

parts.note: B is the second grade after A
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: A warning not to choose a second-class mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from choosing, especially to decline to vote.

clue.text: Clue for a laugh in 30 minutes?

definitions.meaning: take half of the word hour and you get ho, a laugh

explanation.surface: Looking for a laugh within half an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty minutes is half of an hour; and the instruction to halve hour leaves a laughing ho.

clue.text: Stone in bitter fruit is on the outside

indicators.note: the fruit sits around the little word in

parts.note: olives are bitter fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stone inside a bitter fruit is on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green mineral, used as a gemstone called peridot.

clue.text: Clear result of deflated ego?

parts.note: something deflated is limp
the id, like the ego, is a Freudian part of the mind

explanation.surface: Clarity as the outcome of an ego taken down a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid means clear, as in clear water or prose.

clue.text: Dark isles represented in computer accessory

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: Dark islands are depicted in a computer add-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser disk is an optical storage disc used with computers.

clue.text: Get in a strop about new cooker

indicators.note: the fury surrounds the letter for new

parts.note: to rage is to get in a strop, British slang for a sulky temper

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross about a new oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove, a cooker.

clue.text: Sign tooth rot's not starting

indicators.note: the first letter of the decay is dropped

parts.note: caries is tooth decay

explanation.surface: A sign that tooth decay hasn't begun.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Lover in third from last wagon

indicators.note: the third letter of the word last is taken

parts.note: a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A lover rides in the third wagon from the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third from last' looks like counting back; it means the third letter of 'last', S.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a young suitor or lover in pastoral poetry.

clue.text: I predict a terrible crime

indicators.note: a terrible version of the words, badly rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortune teller foresees a dreadful crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricide, killing one's father, is a crime.

clue.text: Ended with pertinent broadcast that's linked

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are spread about

explanation.surface: A broadcast finished with something relevant and connected.
explanation.definitionFit: Interdependent things rely on each other, so they are linked.
